title: Azure Monitor Insights, Network Watcher and Connection Monitor
learningObjective: Configure and interpret VM insights, Storage insights and Network insights, and use Network Watcher and Connection Monitor to monitor connectivity.
foundation: Insights are ready-made monitoring experiences for a type of resource: VMs, storage accounts, networks, containers and more.
Network Watcher diagnoses and monitors network connectivity; Connection Monitor tests connections continuously.
engineer: VM insights: enable on VMs/scale sets (installs Azure Monitor Agent and a DCR sending performance data to a workspace; the optional Map feature adds dependency data). Shows CPU, memory, disk and network trends, top N machines and processes/connections.
Storage insights: built from storage platform metrics, no setup: capacity, availability, transactions, end-to-end and server latency, failures by type across accounts.
Network insights: topology and health of network resources (gateways, load balancers, VNets), with links to resource-specific insights and Connection Monitor results.
Network Watcher tools: topology, IP flow verify, NSG diagnostics, next hop, effective security rules, connection troubleshoot, packet capture, VPN troubleshoot, VNet flow logs and Traffic analytics.

Connection Monitor: test groups of sources (Azure VMs with the Network Watcher agent extension, Arc-enabled or on-premises machines with Azure Monitor Agent) and destinations (IP, FQDN, Azure resources) using TCP, HTTP or ICMP test configurations with thresholds for checks failed % and round-trip time. Results go to Log Analytics and can trigger alerts.

example.title: Watching the on-premises link
body: Connection Monitor tests TCP 443 from three Azure VMs to an on-premises ERP server every 30 seconds with thresholds of 5% failed checks and 100 ms RTT. When the VPN degrades, the test state turns Fail and the ops action group is alerted; the topology view shows the failing hop.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Monitoring Contributor (alerts, diagnostic settings) or Backup Contributor (vaults, policies)
limits: See Azure Monitor / Azure Backup service limits
portal: Monitor > Virtual Machines (VM insights) > Configure insights: choose a DCR and workspace.
Monitor > Storage accounts (Storage insights): review failures and latency.
Network Watcher > Connection monitor > Create: sources, destinations, test configuration, thresholds, alerting.
configuration.cli:
az vm extension set -g rg-app --vm-name vm-app -n NetworkWatcherAgentLinux --publisher Microsoft.Azure.NetworkWatcher
az network watcher connection-monitor create -n cm-erp --location eastus --endpoint-source-name vm-app --endpoint-source-resource-id $VM_ID --endpoint-dest-name erp --endpoint-dest-address erp.contoso.local --test-config-name tcp443 --protocol Tcp --tcp-port 443 --frequency 30 --threshold-failed-percent 5 --threshold-round-trip-time 100
configuration.powershell:
Set-AzVMExtension -ResourceGroupName rg-app -VMName vm-app -Name NetworkWatcherAgentWindows -Publisher Microsoft.Azure.NetworkWatcher -Type NetworkWatcherAgentWindows -TypeHandlerVersion 1.4
Get-AzNetworkWatcherConnectionMonitor -Location eastus

lab.objective: Pick the right Insight or Network Watcher tool and set up Connection Monitor.
steps: Insights and Network Watcher: answer every requirement.
Connection Monitor: run the default (no agent).
Apply 'Install the agent', then 'Latency degradation' and 'Destination down'.
expected: Connection Monitor needs an agent on sources

validation.text: Saw a threshold breach raise an alert

failureScenarios: No agent on the source VM
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: No DCR association or agent not reporting.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the agent extension and Heartbeat table.

troubleshooting.cause: Network Watcher agent missing or Network Watcher not enabled in the region.
troubleshooting.fix: Install the extension; enable Network Watcher.

troubleshooting.symptom: Storage insights shows high server latency.
troubleshooting.fix: Investigate request patterns; E2E vs server latency difference indicates client/network.

comparisons.service: CloudWatch Container/Lambda Insights and VPC Reachability Analyzer

comparisons.difference: Connection Monitor is continuous; IP flow verify/next hop are point-in-time.

misconceptions.myth: Connection Monitor works without anything on the VM.
misconceptions.reality: Azure VM sources need the Network Watcher agent extension.

architectureDecisions: Enable VM insights through Azure Policy for all production VMs.
Monitor critical hybrid paths with Connection Monitor and alert on thresholds.

walkthrough.subtitle: Use ready-made monitoring views for VMs, storage and networks, and watch a network path continuously.
learn: VM insights and what it needs

steps.label: Where to look
steps.title: Too many charts, no overview
body: You want a dashboard per service type that shows the important numbers, without building it yourself.

steps.label: Insights
steps.title: Insights are curated monitoring views
body: Azure Monitor Insights give ready-made workbooks for a service type: VM insights, Storage insights, Network insights, Container insights and more.

steps.label: VM insights
steps.title: VM insights
body: Enable it on a VM or scale set: it installs the Azure Monitor Agent and a data collection rule, sending data to a Log Analytics workspace. You get performance charts (CPU, memory, disk) and optionally a Map of processes and connections.

steps.label: Storage + network
steps.title: Storage and Network insights
body: Storage insights use platform metrics, so they work without setup: capacity, transactions, availability and latency across accounts. Network insights show the health and topology of your network resources.

steps.label: Network Watcher
steps.title: Network Watcher's toolbox
body: Per-region service with diagnostic tools: IP flow verify, Next hop, Effective security rules, Connection troubleshoot, Packet capture, VPN troubleshoot, Topology, and VNet flow logs.

steps.label: Connection monitor
steps.title: Connection monitor watches a path
body: Connection monitor runs tests continuously from sources (Azure VMs or on-premises machines with the agent) to destinations (VMs, URLs, IPs) on a port. It records failed checks and round-trip time and can raise alerts when thresholds are crossed.

callout.text: Connection troubleshoot = one-off check. Connection monitor = continuous.

handsOn.title: Turn on VM insights and a connection monitor
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. Insights data in Log Analytics adds cents.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A small Linux VM vm-lab in rg-az104-lab: Virtual machines > + Create, Ubuntu 24.04, Standard_B1s, password authentication, public inbound ports None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead. Monitoring agents, Azure Backup and Site Recovery all need to reach Azure services.

steps.do: Open vm-lab > Monitoring > Insights > Enable. Choose Azure Monitor Agent, data collection rule: create new, workspace: create or pick one. Configure.
steps.see: Deployment of the agent and DCR. Data appears after about 10 minutes.
Charts for CPU, available memory, logical disk space and network.

steps.do: Search 'Monitor' > Insights > Storage accounts (if you have one) or Networks.
Search 'Network Watcher' > Monitoring > Connection monitor > + Create. Name cm-lab, region your region.
Add a test group: source vm-lab; destination: external address www.microsoft.com; test configuration HTTP or TCP port 443, every 30 seconds. Create.
steps.see: cm-lab listed. Results after a few minutes.
Checks failed % and round-trip time from vm-lab to the destination. (Fails if the subnet has no outbound internet: that is useful to see too.)

check: VM insights shows performance data; cm-lab reports checks.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
